questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, highlighters, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE ON ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet. Calculators may be used.
purchased an item to be used by the business for more than 12 months
took goods for resale for his own use
transferred his own vehicle to the business Which items are capital expenditure?

options.A: 1 and 2 B 2 and 3 C 2 only D 3 and 4

questions.questionText: At the beginning of the year a business has a provision for doubtful debts of $2600. At the year end the provision is to be 5% of trade receivables. The balance on the sales ledger control account at the year end is $69200, before writing off a bad debt of $480. The business operates a separate bad debts account. What is the entry in the income statement for the provision for doubtful debts?

options.A: $836 credit B $836 debit C $860 credit D $860 debit

questions.questionText: The table below shows how a non-current asset appears in the statement of financial position. $ non-current asset at cost 120000 accumulated depreciation (18000) net book value 102000 The asset is revalued to $136000. What is the journal entry to record the revaluation? debit credit $ $

options.A: non-current asset at cost 16000 income statement 16000
options.B: non-current asset at cost 16000 accumulated depreciation 18000 revaluation reserve 34000
options.C: non-current asset at cost 34000 revaluation reserve 34000
options.D: non-current asset at cost 16000 revaluation reserve 16000

questions.questionText: A vehicle was part exchanged for a new vehicle. Which entries record the part exchange? account debited account credited
Which transaction would increase the current assets of a business?

options.B: purchasing a non-current asset on credit for $5000
options.C: purchasing inventory on credit for $1000 and selling immediately for $2000 cash
options.D: selling inventory of $1000 at cost price on credit

questions.questionText: A business has a bank balance of $4800. It pays for materials invoiced at $3000 less trade discount of 30% and cash discount of 10%. A cheque for $450 is received from a customer. What is the bank balance after these transactions?
A sole trader pays private expenses from the business bank account and records them as drawings. Which accounting principle is applied?

A draft statement of financial position shows a bank balance of $1400. The following information is now available. $ cheques issued but not yet cleared by the bank 150 bank charges not in the cash book 45 lodgements in the cash book but not on the bank statement 220 Which figure is shown on the bank statement?
A suspense account showed the following. suspense account $ $ purchases 300 balance b/d 120 Judy 180 300 300 The business did not maintain control accounts. Which errors had been made? purchases Judy

options.A: purchases journal had credit sales of $460 had been been overcast by $300 entered as $640 in Judy’s account
options.B: purchases journal had credit sales of $640 had been been overcast by $300 entered as $460 in Judy’s account
options.C: purchases journal had credit sales of $460 had been been undercast by $300 entered as $640 in Judy’s account
options.D: purchases journal had credit sales of $640 had been been undercast by $300 entered as $460 in Judy’s account

questions.questionText: At the start of the year a business had the opening trade payables of $13000. At the end of the year it owed $15000 to trade payables. During the year it paid them $190000, after taking a cash discount of $10000. What was the amount of the credit purchases for the year?
Which error must be corrected by a one-sided journal entry?

options.A: a cheque entered in the cash book but not posted in a ledger account
options.B: a contra entry in the sales ledger control account not entered in the purchases ledger control account
options.C: an error in the total value of sales ledger balances included in the trial balance
options.D: discount allowed entered in a customer’s account but not entered in the discount column in the cash book

questions.questionText: A trader uses his bank statements and paying in books to produce a summary of his receipts and payments for the year. Why does he do this?

options.A: in order to calculate his closing inventory
options.B: in order to prepare a bank reconciliation statement
options.C: to be able to calculate total sales and total purchases
options.D: to know the amount of bad debts written off

questions.questionText: A trader has two departments in his clothes store – men’s and women’s. The following information is available. men’s women’s sales staff (number) 7 13 floor space 81m2 99m2 value of non-current assets $90000 $135000 annual sales $247000 $403000 The cost of advertising and distribution is $68100. What is the cost for advertising and distribution for the men’s department?

X and Y are in partnership sharing profits equally. They have capital account balances of $30000 and $80000 respectively. Z joins the partnership and pays $10000 for his share of goodwill. The new profit-sharing ratio is 2 : 2 :1. What is the balance on Y’s capital account after Z joins?
On which basis should inventory be valued?

options.B: lower of cost and net realisable value
options.C: lower of cost and replacement cost

questions.questionText: A vehicle cost $12000 and its estimated residual value was $2000. The vehicle was depreciated at 25% per annum using the straight line method. After three years the vehicle was sold for $3500. What was the profit or loss on disposal?

options.A: $500 profit B $1000 loss C $1000 profit D $4500 loss

questions.questionText: What do the reserves of limited companies include?
Which stakeholder in a limited company has a voting right?

Peter is a sole trader whose business is profitable. He is considering going into partnership with Axel, another sole trader, to improve his liquidity. Which figure from Axel’s financial statements is of particular interest to Peter?

The profit margins of a company over two years showed the following. 31 March 31 March year 1 year 2 gross profit margin 37.2% 39.1% net profit margin 12.2% 11.8% Which combination of factors could have caused these changes?

options.A: a change in the combination of goods sold leading to lower selling costs
options.B: a loss of trade discounts on purchases but an increase in cash discounts taken from suppliers
options.C: an advertising campaign to promote higher sales leading to higher selling prices
options.D: an increase in both production and selling costs

questions.questionText: The following information has been extracted from the statement of financial position of a limited company. $ 6% debenture (2016 – 2018) 20000 ordinary share capital issued – 400000 ordinary shares of $1 each 400000 5% preference shares of $1 each 200000 share premium account 50000 retained earnings 75000 What is the value of the shareholders’ equity?

A company has the following items on its statement of financial position. $000 ordinary shares 12000 10% preference shares 5000 retained earnings 7000 The company had made a profit of $5000000 of which $2000000 is paid in dividends, including $500000 paid to preference shareholders. What is the return on capital employed?
A business provides the following financial information. $ opening inventory 24000 closing inventory 32000 cost of sales 140000 sales 220000 What is the inventory turnover?

options.A: 47 days B 54 days C 73 days D 84 days

questions.questionText: A business finds that its profit for 2012 is the same whether marginal costing or absorption costing is used. What does this mean?

options.A: Inventories have been written down to zero value in the period.
options.B: Inventories have decreased during the period.
options.C: Inventories have increased during the period.
options.D: Inventories have stayed the same during the period.

questions.questionText: A baker receives one order for 350 loaves of bread. Which costing method will the baker use?

A company manufactures and sells chairs. The following financial information is available. per unit $ selling price 25 direct material and labour 12 other variable production costs 3 variable selling costs 2 fixed costs 4 The company has the option of buying in the chairs for resale instead of making them. At which purchase price would the company’s profit be unchanged?

Purchases in January 2014 are expected to be $20000 and to increase by $1000 each month. 20% of purchases are for cash. Credit purchases are paid for in the month following purchase. Which amount will be shown in the cash budget for payments to credit suppliers in March 2014?
